lead: A second writer can replace a file you created *this session*, and the only notice is a "changed on disk" line.
body: Two concurrent runs of one slice produce two implementations of the same new module and two conformance cases for it, and the second Write silently wins. Do not revert — the tree is only consistent with the newer one — but re-read the file before every later edit, delete the duplicate case rather than shipping both, and look for it in the `git status --short` you run before staging, which is the only place it shows.
